title: Higher direct images of modules as sheafified cohomology of preimages; stalks
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $p\ge0$, with higher direct image $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is the sheaf associated [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] to the presheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal P_p:V\mapsto H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}(V)})$ ($\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through $f^\sharp:\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$), whose restriction maps are the restrictions of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b); that is, there is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\theta:\mathcal P_p\to R^pf_*\mathcal F$ which is universal among morphisms to sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. ($\theta$ is the canonical map: for an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, it sends the class in $H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)=H^p(\mathcal I^\bullet(f^{-1}V))$ of a cocycle $s\in\mathcal I^p(f^{-1}V)=(f_*\mathcal I^p)(V)$ to the section over $V$ of $\mathcal H^p(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=R^pf_*\mathcal F$ defined by $s$.) Consequently, for $y\in Y$ the induced map $\theta_y:\varinjlim_{V\ni y}H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)\to(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$ from the stalk of the presheaf to the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules. For $p=0$, $R^0f_*\mathcal F=f_*\mathcal F$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 01E4 (lemma-describe-higher-direct-images, line 590), with Sheaves, Lemma 007Z (sheaves-lemma-stalk-sheafification) for the stalks

proof.text: (Injective resolution; $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ as the cohomology of $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$.) $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], so $\mathcal F$ has an injective resolution $s:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ with $\mathcal I^q=0$ for $q<0$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1). The direct image $f_*:\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, $(f_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)$ with $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through $f^\sharp$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], is additive and left exact, since kernels and finite direct sums of modules are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $f_*$ is sectionwise the identity on $\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)$. $R^pf_*$ is its $p$-th right derived functor [pqf-def-cohomology], so there is an isomorphism $\iota^p_{\mathcal I}:R^pf_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^p(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$, the $p$-th cohomology of the complex $f_*\mathcal I^0\to f_*\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ in the abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, compatible with the maps induced by morphisms of resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. For $p=0$, $f_*(s)$ induces an isomorphism $f_*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2), whence $R^0f_*\mathcal F\cong f_*\mathcal F$.

source.place: Lemma 01E4 (lemma-describe-higher-direct-images, line 590), proof, first sentence ('R^if_*F is by definition the i-th cohomology sheaf of the complex f_*I^0 -> f_*I^1 -> ...'); Section 01DH/Theorem 01DU for the injective resolution

proof.text: (Cohomology over an open $U\subseteq X$ from the same resolution.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be open (in the application $U=f^{-1}(V)$, an open subscheme). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives], $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, with $\mathcal I^q|_U=0$ for $q<0$. $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)$ is the $p$-th right derived functor of the left exact functor $\Gamma(U,-)$ on $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], so [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] gives an isomorphism $\kappa_U:H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(U,\mathcal I^\bullet|_U))=H^p(\mathcal I^\bullet(U))$, using $(\mathcal I^q|_U)(U)=\mathcal I^q(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]; it is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear, the module structure on $H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)$ being the action on the global sections of an injective resolution [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].

source.place: Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 495) and its proof: 'F|_U -> I^bullet|_U is an injective resolution in Mod(O_U). Hence H^p(U,F|_U) is equal to H^p(Gamma(U,I^bullet|_U))'

proof.text: (The restriction maps are induced by restricting the resolution.) Let $U'\subseteq U$ be opens of $X$, $j:U'\to U$ the inclusion, and $\mathrm{res}^U_{U'}:H^p(U,\mathcal F|_U)\to H^p(U',\mathcal F|_{U'})$ the restriction of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) for the scheme $U$ and the $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal G=\mathcal F|_U$ (so $\mathcal G|_{U'}=\mathcal F|_{U'}$, both having sections $\mathcal F(W)$ over $W\subseteq U'$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]). Compute it with the following admissible choices in that definition: $\mathcal J^\bullet=\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ for $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U'}$ for $\mathcal G|_{U'}$ (injective resolutions by Step 2); $\mathcal J'^\bullet=j_*(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U'})$, a complex of injective $\mathcal O_U$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives] (3), with $\lambda=\mathrm{id}$ (trivially a quasi-isomorphism); and $\beta=\rho_{\mathcal I}:\mathcal I^\bullet|_U\to j_*(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U'})$, the restriction maps $\mathcal I^q(W)\to\mathcal I^q(W\cap U')$, a morphism of complexes since the differentials commute with restriction. The required identity $\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0\circ j_*(s|_{U'})\circ\rho_{\mathcal G}$ says $s(t)|_{W\cap U'}=s(t|_{W\cap U'})$ for $t\in\mathcal F(W)$, which holds because $s$ is a morphism of sheaves. Then $\mu=\Gamma(U,\lambda)$ is the identity of $\Gamma(U,j_*(\mathcal I^\bullet|_{U'}))=\mathcal I^\bullet(U')$, and $\mathrm{res}^U_{U'}=H^p(\Gamma(U,\beta))$ is the map induced on $H^p$ by the restriction $\mathcal I^\bullet(U)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(U')$. By independence of the choices [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (1) this is $\mathrm{res}^U_{U'}$ for any choices; so under the isomorphisms $\kappa_U,\kappa_{U'}$ of Step 2, $\mathrm{res}^U_{U'}$ is $H^p$ of the restriction maps of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ (Stacks' equation 01E2).

source.place: Equation 01E2 (equation-restriction-mapping, lines 527-555): the restriction H^n(V,F) -> H^n(U,F) is induced by the restriction maps Gamma(V,I^bullet) -> Gamma(U,I^bullet); the comparison with the DAG's definition [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) is written by the agent

proof.text: (The presheaf of sections of $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$.) By the definition of $f_*$ (Step 1), $(f_*\mathcal I^q)(V)=\mathcal I^q(f^{-1}V)$ with $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through $f^\sharp$, the differentials of $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ over $V$ are those of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ over $f^{-1}V$, and the restriction along $V'\subseteq V$ is the restriction $\mathcal I^\bullet(f^{-1}V)\to\mathcal I^\bullet(f^{-1}V')$. Hence the presheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\mathcal Q_p:V\mapsto H^p((f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)(V))=\Ker(\mathcal I^p(f^{-1}V)\to\mathcal I^{p+1}(f^{-1}V))/\Im(\mathcal I^{p-1}(f^{-1}V)\to\mathcal I^p(f^{-1}V))$ is, via the isomorphisms $\kappa_{f^{-1}V}$ of Step 2 (which are $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear, being $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$-linear) and Step 3 with $U=f^{-1}V$, $U'=f^{-1}V'$, isomorphic as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules to $\mathcal P_p:V\mapsto H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V})$ with the restriction maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b).

source.place: Lemma 01E4, proof: 'this is obviously equal to Ker(I^i(f^{-1}V) -> I^{i+1}(f^{-1}V))/Im(...) which is equal to H^i(f^{-1}(V),F)'

proof.text: (The cohomology sheaf of a complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules is the sheafified presheaf cohomology.) Let $\mathcal K^\bullet=f_*\mathcal I^\bullet$, a complex in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, and $\iota:\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ the inclusion. In $\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ cohomology is computed sectionwise, so the $p$-th cohomology presheaf of $\iota\mathcal K^\bullet$ is $\mathcal Q_p$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] (1). Sheafification $\#$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] is exact (ibid. (2)), so it commutes with cohomology of complexes [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]: $\mathcal H^p(\#\iota\mathcal K^\bullet)\cong(\mathcal Q_p)^\#$, compatibly with the inclusions of cycles and the projections onto cohomology. Since $\#\circ\iota\cong\mathrm{id}$ (ibid. (3)), $\#\iota\mathcal K^\bullet\cong\mathcal K^\bullet$ and $\mathcal H^p(\mathcal K^\bullet)\cong(\mathcal Q_p)^\#$. Composing the unit $\mathcal Q_p\to\iota(\mathcal Q_p)^\#$ with this isomorphism gives a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\vartheta:\mathcal Q_p\to\iota\mathcal H^p(\mathcal K^\bullet)$ that is universal among maps to sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; by the compatibility with cycles it sends the class of a cocycle $z\in\Ker(d^p)(V)=\Ker(d^p_V)$ (kernels being sectionwise) to the image of $z$ under the projection $\Ker d^p\to\mathcal H^p(\mathcal K^\bullet)$.

source.place: Lemma 01E4, proof: 'By definition of the abelian category structure on O_Y-modules this cohomology sheaf is the sheaf associated to the presheaf V -> Ker(f_*I^i(V) -> f_*I^{i+1}(V))/Im(f_*I^{i-1}(V) -> f_*I^i(V))'; with Modules, Section 01AF (kernels sectionwise, cokernels sheafified)

proof.text: (Conclusion: $R^pf_*\mathcal F=\mathcal P_p^\#$.) Put $\theta=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ\vartheta\circ\kappa^{-1}:\mathcal P_p\to R^pf_*\mathcal F$, with $\kappa:\mathcal Q_p\cong\mathcal P_p$ of Step 4, $\vartheta$ of Step 5 and $\iota^p_{\mathcal I}$ of Step 1. It is the canonical map of the statement, and it is universal among morphisms from $\mathcal P_p$ to sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules because $\vartheta$ is and $\kappa$, $\iota^p_{\mathcal I}$ are isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. It does not depend on the injective resolution: for a second resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ and a morphism of complexes $\varphi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal F}$, the maps $\iota^p$, $\kappa_U$ for the two resolutions differ by $H^p$ of $f_*\varphi$, resp. $\varphi(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift], and $\vartheta$, being natural in the complex, commutes with $f_*\varphi$; so the two maps $\theta$ agree.

source.place: Lemma 01E4, proof, last line ('and we win')

proof.text: (Stalks.) Let $\eta:\mathcal P_p\to\mathcal P_p^\#$ be the sheafification as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Both $\eta$ and $\theta$ (Step 6) are universal, so there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\psi:\mathcal P_p^\#\to R^pf_*\mathcal F$ with $\psi\circ\eta=\theta$, and $\theta_y=\psi_y\circ\eta_y$ on stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The underlying map of abelian presheaves of $\eta$ is the sheafification of the underlying abelian presheaf of $\mathcal P_p$ [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], so $\eta_y:(\mathcal P_p)_y\to(\mathcal P_p^\#)_y$ is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space]; $\psi_y$ is bijective with inverse $(\psi^{-1})_y$. Both are $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-linear, being induced by morphisms of presheaves of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Hence $\theta_y:\varinjlim_{V\ni y}H^p(f^{-1}V,\mathcal F)=(\mathcal P_p)_y\to(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks Cohomology Lemma 01E4 and its proof (cohomology.tex:590-627), with Lemma 01E1 and Equation 01E2 (lines 495-555) and Sheaves 007Z, into seven steps: (1) enough injectives in Mod(O_X), injective resolution, R^pf_*F = H^p(f_*I) via lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift, and R^0f_* = f_*; (2) I|_U is an injective resolution of F|_U (new node lem-weil-pbc-module-open-restriction-injectives, Stacks 01E1(1) + 02N5), so H^p(U,F|_U) = H^p(I(U)); (3) the restriction maps of def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap (b) are induced by restriction of I (choices J' = j_*(I|_{U'}), lambda = id, beta = restriction; agent-written comparison, Stacks 01E2); (4) (f_*I)(V) = I(f^{-1}V), so the presheaf cohomology of f_*I is the presheaf P_p; (5) the cohomology sheaf of a complex of O_Y-modules is the sheafified presheaf cohomology (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact: PMod(O_X) abelian sectionwise, sheafification exact, counit iso; with the existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology); (6) conclusion and independence of the resolution; (7) stalks via lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space (Mathlib leaf). The site version lem-weil-pbc-site-higher-direct-image-sheafified-presheaf (072W) is not used: it is stated for abelian sheaves, and R^pf_* here is derived in Mod(O_X) -> Mod(O_Y); using it would need the comparison of module and abelian derived functors, longer than the direct proof.
